newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks fall in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks fall in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange fell on Sunday amid pessimism among investors over the market's shorter term outlook, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index shed 0.17 percent to 148.50 points on Sunday in thin turnover worth 406,914 dinars ($574,737).
"The market is weak and only some improvement on Jordan Cement Factories...with overall activity very quiet with nothing new to help bring any renewed impetus," said one trader.

Dealers say the market, already hit by a tight monetary policy that has diverted small investors to higher yield instruments, is additionally being hurt by continued uncertainty over Middle East peace talks.
The market has remained in a wait-and-see mood since the recent flareup in violence in Palestinian self-rule areas.

Dealers said speculative trade on Livestock and Poultry, which has dominated recent turnover appears to have petered out. The stock, which brokers say has been taken over by a single investor in recent weeks, fell another 0.01 dinars to 0.62 dinars with only 19,250 shares changing hands.
In otherwise lacklustre trade, two key industrial shares continued to be the focus of limited outside buying, which brokers say could be foreign funds.

Blue-chip Jordan Cement Factories, in which Jordan wants to divest a 20 percent share, improved for the second day in a row to 3.38 dinars, a 0.30 dinars rise. Leading ready made garments manufacturer El-Zay rose 0.02 dinars to 1.86 dinars.
Market heavyweight Arab Bank, a major component in the official index, shed 2.00 dinars to 247 dinars on a low 140 share turnover, helping drag the market down.
Overall 20 stocks fell on Sunday, eleven were unchanged and only nine rose.

The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.14 percent to 80.67 points from 80.78 points on Saturday, still 15.54 percent down from the same time last year.
A total of 124,353 shares worth 74,683 dinars changed hands in dull trade in the parallel market.
